specification.problem: Perfect state transfer (PST) of an arbitrary unknown qubit state between two sites of a lattice using a discrete-time quantum walk (DTQW) whose coin operation may vary with time step and position ('various settings of coin flippings'). The abstract claims PST of an arbitrary unknown two-qubit state, extension to multi-qubit entangled-state distribution on a multi-dimensional network, and quantum routing; it gives no equations, encodings, or coin schedules.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction chosen here (an assumption, not the paper's protocol): a single DTQW walker on a one-dimensional line with a two-dimensional coin, transferring ONE unknown coin qubit from site 0 to site d using a position- and time-dependent coin schedule drawn from {I, X}. Tiny explicit instance: d = 2, T = d + 2 = 4 steps, positions in [-1, 3] (encoded as y = x + 1 in 3 qubits) plus one coin qubit. Outside scope: the paper's two-qubit (coin + position or two-walker) encoding, its specific coin-flipping settings, the multi-dimensional network and multi-qubit entangled-state distribution between every pair of sites, and the routing architecture.

symbols.meaning: walker position (site index) on the one-dimensional line
coin (internal) state label; c=0 moves right, c=1 moves left
amplitude of the walker at site x with coin value c
coin operator applied at time step t to a walker located at site x
one full walk step (position-dependent coin followed by shift) at time t
arbitrary unknown single-qubit state to be transferred, initially carried by the coin
known, state-independent unitary correction on the transferred qubit
symbols.domain: U(2); in the proposed schedule V = X

symbols.meaning: shifted non-negative position label for register encoding, y = x + 1
symbols.domain: \{0,\dots,d+2\}, stored as an n_P-bit unsigned integer

equations.label: DTQW state space
equations.description: The walker lives on a position register tensored with a two-level coin register.
equations.justification: Standard definition of a coined discrete-time quantum walk on a line.
assumptions: One walker, two-dimensional coin, one-dimensional line (the paper's network is multi-dimensional).

equations.label: Coin-conditioned shift
equations.description: Coin value 0 moves the walker one site to the right, coin value 1 one site to the left.
equations.justification: Standard flip-flop-free shift of the coined DTQW; direction convention chosen here.

equations.label: Walk step with position- and time-dependent coin flippings
equations.latex: U_t = S \Big( \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}} |x\rangle\langle x| \otimes C_t(x) \Big), \qquad C_t(x) \in \{I, X\}
equations.description: Each step applies a coin operator that may depend on the site and the step, then shifts. The restriction to {I, X} ('flipping' vs 'no flipping') is an interpretation.
equations.abstract_quote: via a discrete-time quantum walk with various settings of coin flippings
equations.justification: The abstract says PST is achieved by varying the coin flippings; the natural formalisation is a site- and step-dependent coin inside the standard DTQW step. The exact coin set used in the paper is not stated.
assumptions: Coin set restricted to {I, X}; the paper may use other coins (e.g. Hadamard) in some settings.

equations.label: Perfect state transfer condition
equations.latex: U_T U_{T-1} \cdots U_1 \big( |0\rangle_P \otimes |\phi\rangle_C \big) = |d\rangle_P \otimes V|\phi\rangle_C \quad \forall\, |\phi\rangle \in \mathbb{C}^2, \; V \text{ fixed, independent of } |\phi\rangle
equations.description: After T steps the walker is found at site d with certainty and the unknown qubit is recovered up to a known unitary V (exact equality, not approximate).
equations.abstract_quote: a perfect state transfer of an arbitrary unknown two-qubit state can be achieved
equations.justification: 'Perfect' and 'arbitrary unknown' imply unit-fidelity, input-independent (hence linear/unitary) transfer; here specialised from the paper's two-qubit claim to a single coin qubit.
assumptions: Specialisation to one qubit; the paper's two-qubit encoding is unknown.

equations.label: Proposed coin schedule (assumption)
equations.latex: C_1(x) = I;\quad C_2(x) = \begin{cases} X & x=-1 \\ I & \text{else}\end{cases};\quad C_t(x) = I \;(3 \le t \le T-1);\quad C_T(x) = \begin{cases} X & x = T-2 \\ I & \text{else}\end{cases};\quad T = d+2
equations.description: Step 1 splits the two coin components to x=\pm1; step 2 flips the left component so both travel right with separation 2; the final step flips the leading component so both components meet at x = T-2 = d.
equations.justification: A minimal explicit schedule constructed here that satisfies eq_4 using only {I,X} coins; it is not taken from the paper.
assumptions: Not the paper's schedule; chosen as the smallest construction consistent with eq_3 and eq_4.

equations.label: Resulting transfer for the proposed schedule
equations.latex: U_T\cdots U_1\big(|0\rangle \otimes (a|0\rangle + b|1\rangle)\big) = |d\rangle \otimes (a|1\rangle + b|0\rangle) = |d\rangle \otimes X|\phi\rangle, \qquad d = T-2
equations.description: Trajectory: after step 1: a|1,0\rangle + b|-1,1\rangle; after step 2: a|2,0\rangle + b|0,0\rangle; after step t (3 \le t \le T-1): a|t,0\rangle + b|t-2,0\rangle; after step T: a|T-2,1\rangle + b|T-2,0\rangle. Hence V = X in eq_4. For d=2, T=4.
equations.justification: Direct application of eq_2, eq_3 and eq_5 to the initial state; derived here, not verified against the paper.
assumptions: Infinite line or a register large enough that positions in [-1, d+1] do not wrap; d \ge 1.

registers.name: P (position)
registers.size: n_P = \lceil \log_2(d+3) \rceil qubits (3 qubits for d=2), storing y = x+1 \in \{0,\dots,d+2\} as an unsigned big-endian integer
registers.role: Walker position on the line; site 0 is the sender, site d the receiver.

registers.name: C (coin)
registers.role: Coin register; initially carries the unknown qubit |\phi\rangle and delivers X|\phi\rangle at the end.

specification.initial_state: |\Psi_0\rangle = |x=0\rangle_P \otimes (a|0\rangle + b|1\rangle)_C, i.e. position register in |y=1\rangle (binary 001 for n_P=3) and coin in the unknown state |\phi\rangle.

steps.description: Prepare the position register in |x=0\rangle (y=1) and load the unknown qubit |\phi\rangle into the coin register.
Step t=1: apply coin I everywhere, then the shift S; the two coin components separate to x=+1 and x=-1.
Step t=2: apply X on the coin controlled on position x=-1 (y=0), I elsewhere, then S; both components now have coin 0 and sit at x=2 and x=0.
Steps t=3,...,T-1: coin I everywhere followed by S; both components move right in parallel, at x=t and x=t-2.
Step t=T=d+2: apply X on the coin controlled on position x=T-2 (the leading component), I elsewhere, then S; the components recombine at x=d with the coin in X|\phi\rangle.
Apply the known correction V^\dagger = X to the coin register (or absorb it into the receiver's basis relabelling) to recover |\phi\rangle at site d.

specification.measurement: Verification only (the protocol itself is unitary): measure the position register in the computational basis; outcome y = d+1 (x=d) should occur with probability 1. The coin register, after the X correction, should equal |\phi\rangle; verify by state tomography or by measuring in the basis that distinguishes |\phi\rangle for several known test inputs (e.g. |0\rangle, |1\rangle, |+\rangle, |+i\rangle) and estimating fidelity.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Check that all position outcomes equal x=d; estimate transfer fidelity F = |\langle\phi| X \rho_C X |\phi\rangle| from tomography of the coin register over the test inputs; F should be exactly 1 in a noiseless simulation.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the single-qubit line transfer with d=2, T=4 was chosen as the smallest useful instance and is not claimed to be the paper's protocol.
Coin operators restricted to {I, X} as an interpretation of 'coin flippings'.
Shift convention c=0 -> x+1, c=1 -> x-1; position register large enough to avoid wrap-around (positions -1..d+1).
The known final correction V=X is allowed in the definition of perfect state transfer (transfer up to a fixed, input-independent unitary).
missing_information: How the paper encodes a two-qubit state in the walk (e.g. coin plus a position degree of freedom, or two walkers/coins) and the corresponding coin-flipping settings.
The specific coin operators and their time/position schedule used in the paper for PST.
The structure of the multi-dimensional network and the protocol for distributing an arbitrary multi-qubit entangled state between every pair of sites.
The routing scheme (how paths/targets are selected by coin settings) and any resource counts (number of steps vs. distance/dimension).
Any statements about robustness, measurement scheme, or physical implementation.
